This intelligent question was raised by @OgechiMiracle4 as comment under my Day 10 post, and I'll be glad to explain to the Bless community at large.

Most people don’t realize this... ✴️

When you run a node on @theblessnetwork , you're not just “mining” or staking, you’re literally powering a shared global computer.

Here's what that actually means 

1️⃣ Apps like AI tools, websites, or games need compute to run, basically, digital “muscle” to process data.

Traditionally, they rent it from AWS or Google Cloud. That’s centralized, expensive, and gatekept.

2️⃣ Bless flips that model.

Instead of one giant data center, it breaks compute into tiny jobs, and spreads them across regular people’s devices (like yours).

Your laptop becomes a mini server.
So does someone’s console in Lagos...or a smart TV in Manila.

3️⃣ When you run a Bless node, you're offering spare processing power from your device to help execute these jobs.

▶️ AI models? Rendered through you.
▶️ Website traffic? Routed through you.
All secured, sandboxed, and privacy-safe.

4️⃣ The more stable and responsive your node, the more work it can take on... and the more $TIME points you earn.

This is compute as a community resource.
It’s like Airbnb for processing power.

5️⃣ The vision?
A truly decentralized internet, not just in theory, but in function. One where everyday people own the infrastructure, not just use it.

You’re not just part of the network.
You are the network.

Please repost 🔁 and educate more people
